configurations.//: THE DEFAULT. A real build without the image: same Postgres, same models, same WASM renderer, same bundled fonts, and `/api/render` returns a byte-identical PDF to the container's. 5 seconds end to end on this Mac — 3s to build, 2s to boot.
configurations.//2: What it does NOT have is LibreOffice and Tesseract, which live in the image and deliberately not on a laptop (ADR-012). So `.doc` ingestion and OCR of a scan fail here and only here. Those two paths, and the last check before a release, belong to the entry below.
configurations.//3: Needs db and llm, which are separate services and cheap: docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.local.yml up -d db llm
configurations.name: hunterready-host

configurations.//: The same build, seen the way a visitor sees it the day pricing opens. `HR_RELEASE=true` is the single switch out of beta: no Beta chip, no 'free while we are in beta' anywhere, paid designs and the mixed axes locked behind a 402, and an anonymous visitor's CV read on our own machine.
configurations.//2: It exists because the state a switch produces has to be lookable-at before the switch is flipped in production, and this one cannot be rehearsed any other way — `NODE_ENV=development` and `HR_UNLOCK_DESIGNS` both unlock the catalogue, so a laptop always shows the beta view. `HR_RELEASE` deliberately overrides both, and it overrides `HR_THIRD_PARTY_FOR_ALL` too, which is still set in production on purpose.
configurations.//3: 3012 so it can run beside the beta view on 3011 and the two can be compared in two tabs.
configurations.name: hunterready-release

configurations.//: The state production will be in the day pricing opens, which is the one state nobody has ever looked at. `hunterready-release` above shows released-but-unconfigured; this adds the two Stripe variables and Coolify's commit variable, so the pricing card shows `Get Pro` instead of `Paid plans are not open yet` and `/api/health` reports a commit instead of `unknown`.
configurations.//2: The Stripe values are deliberately not credentials and are shaped so a scanner cannot mistake them for any — the same fixtures the tests use. So the button renders and the checkout it starts fails at Stripe with a 502, which is the honest limit of what can be rehearsed without an account: everything up to the network is real, and whether Stripe accepts our payload is plan 01 block 3's verify and needs Edd's keys.
configurations.//3: SOURCE_COMMIT stands in for what Coolify injects. `pnpm host` passes no build arg, so this is also the only local way to exercise the fallback in src/lib/build-stamp.ts — with neither variable, `/api/health` correctly says `unknown` and proves nothing.
configurations.//4: 3013 so it can sit beside beta on 3011 and plain release on 3012.
configurations.name: hunterready-release-configured
runtimeArgs: HR_RELEASE=true STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_fixture_not_a_credential_0000 HR_STRIPE_PRICE_ID=price_fixture_not_a_credential_0000 SOURCE_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD) PORT=3013 pnpm host

configurations.//: The one that ships. Attaches to the real stack — the app image plus Postgres plus the model — started with `pnpm app` (Compose builds `hunterready-app:latest`; NOT `pnpm docker:run`, which starts the app alone with no database and no model, so persistence reports itself off and every generated text silently falls back to regular expressions).
configurations.//2: Reach for it for exactly three things: `.doc` ingestion, OCR of a scan, and confirming the shipping image itself is sound before a release. Otherwise it costs 2 minutes warm and 10+ when the apt layer falls out of cache, for nothing the entry above does not already give you.
configurations.//3: 3100 because Hermes' WhatsApp bridge holds 127.0.0.1:3000 while Docker publishes on *:3000, and a URL that resolves to one of two servers depending on v4/v6 order is not something to debug twice.
configurations.//4: There used to be a third entry here, `hunterready-ui` on 3007: Vite with HMR, proxying /api to this container. It was removed on 2026-08-18 once `pnpm host` was measured at 5 seconds. It saved two of those and required this container to be running to answer a single API call, which is the cost it existed to avoid. What was lost is HMR preserving app state across an edit; if that turns out to matter, bring it back pointing at 3011, not here.
configurations.name: hunterready
